newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom says no brand value in 97 accounts.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says no brand value in 97 accounts.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Thursday that after an exercise in valuing its internally generated brands it had decided it would not try to include such a value in its financial statement for this year.

"An independent valuer has assessed the value of the... brands, however because of current uncertainty over international accounting standards the value of brands is not intended to be included on the Telecom statement of financial position," the company said in a prospectus published today.
Telecom said in February it wanted to see if it could put a value in its consolidated balance sheet as at March 31, 1997.

A spokeswoman said that the logic behind the plan had been to demonstrate the perceived value of the brands to investors, but that the constraints of current US GAAP accounting rules would always have meant that the values could only have been built into a separate balance sheet under New Zealand rules.
Telecom's accounts are currently prepared in one form only, a version of GAAP which applies in New Zealand.
The group will release its accounts for the year to March 31, 1997 on May 14. A brand valuation is due to be included in the supplementary information to these, the prospectus said.
